# API & Backward-Compatibility Checklist: Task Priority

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements governing the extended `GET /api/tasks` contract,
priority/status filter semantics, and backward-compatibility guarantees are complete, clear,
consistent, and objectively verifiable — before implementation proceeds.
**Created**: 2026-09-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md) | [data-model.md](../data-model.md) | [contracts/tasks-api.md](../contracts/tasks-api.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on
feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.
Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is
satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for every priority-filter cardinality (single value, multiple values, and all three selected) rather than only the general "one, several, or all" case? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK002 Does a requirement or contract document specify the exact query parameter name and accepted values for the completion-status filter (e.g., `status=complete`/`incomplete`), rather than leaving the wire format implicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the specific existing response fields that must remain unchanged enumerated anywhere, rather than referenced only generically as "existing fields"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the repeatable-parameter mechanism for selecting multiple priorities (e.g., repeated `priority=` params) stated as a requirement rather than only appearing as a design choice in research/contracts? [Completeness, Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is "existing API responses must not break" quantified into a specific, checkable set of guarantees (field set, types, status codes) rather than left as a general principle? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the required behavior fully specified for a client that sends an invalid priority or status value (e.g., an unrecognized string)? [Clarity, Ambiguity]
- [ ] CHK007 Is SC-003's "single filtering action" defined precisely enough to be testable (e.g., one HTTP request vs. one UI interaction)? [Clarity, Spec §SC-003]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Are the create-time "omit priority → defaults to Medium" and edit-time "omit priority → priority is preserved, not reset" behaviors both stated as explicit requirements (not only inferable from an example), and do they avoid contradicting each other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, FR-012]
- [ ] CHK009 Does FR-007 itself state the AND-combination rule for priority + status filters, or does that rule live only in Clarifications/Assumptions — creating a risk that one could be edited without updating the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the existing `GET /api/tasks/completed` endpoint's relationship to the new status filter addressed by a requirement, so the two aren't left to silently diverge over time? [Consistency, Gap]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK011 Can SC-005 ("zero new failures" for clients that omit priority) be objectively measured, or does it need a stated baseline and measurement method? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK012 Is SC-004's "always appearing before" ordering guarantee tied to a requirement that also covers how same-priority tasks are ordered relative to each other? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004, FR-008]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined for a request that combines an unrecognized `sort` value with otherwise-valid priority/status filters? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK014 Does a requirement define the response shape and status code returned when a filter matches zero tasks, beyond the general "shown empty" statement? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements defined for pagination or very large result sets under the new filters, or is that explicitly declared out of scope? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK016 Is the assumption that "no cross-user or admin view is in scope" cross-checked against how ownership scoping is required to interact with the new filter parameters? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, FR-011]
- [ ] CHK017 Is there a requirement covering behavior during a rolling deploy where an older frontend build (not yet sending the new params) talks to the updated API? [Gap, Assumption]

## Ambiguities & Traceability

- [ ] CHK018 Is there a requirement for the response when a caller's filter legitimately matches none of their own tasks vs. when the caller lacks authorization — ensuring the two cases can't be confused? [Gap, Security boundary]
- [ ] CHK019 Is a consistent requirement-ID scheme applied across spec.md, data-model.md, and contracts/tasks-api.md so a reviewer can trace a documented API field or parameter back to its originating FR? [Traceability]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
